questions.question: A developer has Node.js 22 installed and wants to install GitHub Copilot CLI by using npm. Which command should the developer run?

options.text: npm install -g @github/copilot
options.why: Correct. Copilot CLI is published to npm as @github/copilot and is installed globally.

options.text: gh extension install github/gh-copilot
options.why: This installs the older gh copilot extension, which has been replaced by Copilot CLI.

options.text: npm install -g copilot-cli
options.why: This is not the package name of GitHub Copilot CLI.

options.text: npx github-copilot login
options.why: This is not a valid installation command for Copilot CLI.

questions.explanation: The npm package for GitHub Copilot CLI is @github/copilot and requires Node.js 22 or later.

questions.question: You need to run GitHub Copilot CLI in an automated job where no interactive sign-in is possible. Which credential should you provide?

options.text: A fine-grained personal access token with the Copilot Requests permission, stored in the COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
options.why: Correct. Copilot CLI reads a token from COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, and the token must be fine-grained with Copilot Requests.

options.text: A classic personal access token with the repo scope, stored in GH_TOKEN
options.why: Classic personal access tokens are not supported by Copilot CLI.

options.text: The one-time device code displayed by /login
options.why: The device code requires a person to approve it in a browser, which is not possible in an automated job.

options.text: An SSH key added to the GitHub account
options.why: SSH keys authenticate Git operations and are not used to authenticate Copilot CLI requests.

questions.explanation: For non-interactive use, Copilot CLI authenticates with a fine-grained personal access token that has the Copilot Requests permission.

questions.question: Which TWO statements describe GitHub Copilot CLI? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: It runs as an agent in the terminal that can read, edit and create files in a trusted folder.
options.why: Correct. Copilot CLI works on the files in folders that you trust.

options.text: It asks for approval before using a tool, such as running a shell command, that has not been allowed.
options.why: Correct. Copilot CLI requests permission before it uses a new tool unless the tool was allowed in advance.

options.text: It runs only inside the Visual Studio Code integrated terminal.
options.why: Copilot CLI runs in any terminal on macOS, Linux and Windows.

options.text: It can be used without a GitHub account.
options.why: Copilot CLI requires a GitHub account with access to Copilot.

options.text: It cannot be disabled by an organization.
options.why: Organizations can disable Copilot CLI for members by policy.

questions.explanation: Copilot CLI is a terminal agent that works in trusted folders and asks before using tools that have not been approved.

questions.question: During an interactive Copilot CLI session, a developer wants to include the file src/cart.js in the next prompt. What should the developer type?

options.text: explain @src/cart.js
options.why: Correct. The @ prefix adds a file to the context of the prompt.

options.text: explain !src/cart.js
options.why: The ! prefix runs a shell command rather than adding a file.

options.text: explain #file:src/cart.js
options.why: #file is the context syntax for Copilot Chat in the IDE, not for Copilot CLI.

options.text: /context src/cart.js
options.why: /context shows how the context window is being used and does not add a file.

questions.explanation: In Copilot CLI, @path adds a file to the prompt context.

questions.question: A developer starts GitHub Copilot CLI in a newly cloned repository for the first time. What does Copilot CLI ask the developer to do before it works with the files?

options.text: Confirm whether the files in the current folder are trusted
options.why: Correct. On first run in a folder, Copilot CLI asks whether to trust it, for this session or permanently.

options.text: Create a .github/copilot-instructions.md file
options.why: Custom instructions are optional and are not required before Copilot CLI starts.

options.text: Configure an MCP server in mcp-config.json
options.why: MCP servers are optional; the GitHub MCP server is built in.

options.text: Choose a premium model with /model
options.why: Choosing a model is optional; a default model is used if none is selected.

questions.explanation: Copilot CLI asks you to confirm folder trust because it can read, change and run files in that folder.
